newsitem.title: INDIA: India strike marred by stray violence.
newsitem.headline: India strike marred by stray violence.

text.p: A strike on Monday in India's wealthiest state to protest the death of 12 people in a riot ended peacefully, though marred by a few violent incidents, a state official said.
"We will take strict action against whoever takes the law into his own hands, whether big or small," Deputy Chief Minister Gopinath Munde of Maharashtra state told reporters.
Railway services in Bombay, the state's capital, were disrupted for the greater part of the day, even though it was specifically excluded from the strike, officials said.

Opposition parties called a strike in Maharashtra to protest against the killing of 12 people on Friday when police fired to control a riot that began when the statue of a revered social activist was garlanded with shoes.
Activity in Bombay was paralysed over the weekend by a strike call on Saturday. Monday's strike was to protest over the same incident, but Bombay has been excluded.
An opposition leader demanded the arrest of Bal Thackeray, the firebrand chief of the regional Shiv Sena party, which rules the state in coalition with the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

"We are making this demand to the federal government because this government is not in a position to take any decision," Ranjit Deshmukh, president of the state unit of the Congress party, told reporters.
But Munde said later that his government was not planning any action against Thackeray since he had committed no crime.
Two people were injured when police fired two rounds at a rioting mob in Karanja village in Wardha, almost 600 km east of Bombay, Munde said.
At Hingoli village in Parbhani, about 350 km east of Bombay, an angry crowd set fire to a post-office, causing damage estimated at 500,000 rupees.
In Buldhana, 300 kms northwest of Bombay, police used canes to disperse a mob.

"In Bombay there was no tension," Munde said. "The central railway stopped trains between Kurla and Kalyan in view of small public agitations, but we assured the railway authorities of police protection and services were soon restored."
Thousands of the roughly three million commuters who rely on the trains to get to work were stranded.
Protesters gathered at important points along the road and rail routes into the city, officials said. They shouted slogans or threw stones at vehicles whose drivers defied the strike.
City police chief Subhash Malhotra went on television to request citizens to put no faith in wild rumours that swept the city throughout the day.
In the northeastern Bombay suburb of Dombivli, two men were arrested after they attempted to open fire on a police officer, but nobody was injured, Munde added.

State government officials estimated the success rate of the strike as ranging from 30 percent in areas like Kohlapur and Nashik to 60 percent in Sholapur and Raigad. In the coastal districts of Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg it was almost total and in Dhule, it climbed to 90 percent, they said.
Police arrested 9,939 people all over the state in order to prevent them stirring up trouble, officials said.
